name: Cinematic Doodle Thumbnail
purpose: Create emotionally intense, highly readable YouTube thumbnails that preserve the TossExplains cast while using richer thumbnail-only environments, lighting, and depth.

headline.position: top center, integrated into the continuous illustrated scene

integration.mode: embedded in the same full-frame environment
integration.background: Continue the environment, atmosphere, and lighting behind, around, and below the letters.
integration.allowed_overlap: One or two low-contrast environmental forms may rise behind or between letters without obscuring them.

traits: withholds an answer the image cannot give
carries tone (question, alarm, command, or contradiction)
hook_functions: urgent command tied to a fragile object or action
rejection: is a moral, takeaway, or complete explanation
could be swapped for an unrelated phrase without changing the scene
uses abstract jargon, theory label, or category name
names something invisible or impossible to depict
curiosity_power.speed_test: A viewer who understands the question in under half a second is a viewer who clicks.

rules: Use the headline as a second hook, not a repetition of the video title.
Connect the hook to something visible in the frame.
Prefer danger, scarcity, contradiction, consequence, time pressure, or an unresolved outcome.
Create readability through local contrast inside the scene, never through a detached graphic panel.

layout.story_zone: full-frame continuous environment, with the main action in the middle and lower area
layout.bottom_right: visually quiet for the YouTube duration badge

split_comparison.use_only_when: The script contains a genuinely useful numeric, era, or state comparison.

story.core: Show a frozen moment from an unresolved event, not a neutral portrait.
story.source: Use a specific event, action, object, relationship, experiment, or consequence from the script. Prefer literal incidents over generic scenes or decorative metaphors.

curiosity_contract.viewer_question: Define one unanswered question before composing.
curiosity_contract.headline_role: Ask, warn, command, or predict something involving a visible subject.
curiosity_contract.image_role: Confirm the premise and stakes with physical evidence, then add one clue that makes the missing answer more urgent.
curiosity_contract.withhold: Do not reveal the decisive cause, identity, explanation, escape, or outcome.
curiosity_contract.swap_test: If an unrelated headline can replace the chosen headline without changing the scene, reject the concept.

required: one shared question between headline and image
visible evidence that partially answers the headline
a decisive answer that remains hidden
preferred_moments: the instant the danger is discovered
the moment a resource is nearly lost
the moment a character realizes something is wrong
the moment two characters react differently

characters.identity: Attach only the project character sheets used in the prompt and preserve them exactly.
characters.main_face: large enough for the eyes, brows, and mouth to read at phone size
group_rules: Give every visible co-star a readable face and expression.
Give one character the dominant emotional reaction.
Do not request exact crowd counts above five.
Do not alter the mascot's anatomy or identity.

foreground.treatment: darker or warmer than the main subject, partial soft focus, overlaps the midground
foreground.purpose: give the eye a place to enter the frame

midground.treatment: sharpest, most detail, highest light, strongest saturation

background.treatment: 20 to 40 percent lower saturation, 1 to 2 value steps cooler, softer edges

depth_cues: foreground shape overlapping the main subject
atmospheric perspective dropping saturation and value with distance
motivated occlusion by a doorway, branch, window mullion, shoulder, or falling object
dark framing shapes at the edges

atmosphere.haze: low-contrast distant forms rise behind the headline without obscuring it
atmosphere.falloff: warm light spills onto a face or prop with a radial gradient that fades to the cool ambient over 30 to 60 percent of the subject radius
atmosphere.background_softness: soft edges, no hard outlines on the most distant plane

palette_continuity.rule: The headline area, the midground, and the background share one hue gradient.
palette_continuity.failure_mode: Three different palettes across the three planes break the painted-on illusion.
palette_continuity.prefer: one cool dominant family + one warm accent carried through every plane

color.formula: Cool or dark environment, warm brown characters, yellow headline, and one concentrated warm focal light.

lighting.style: cinematic and motivated by a visible source
lighting.corners: quiet and darker than the focal area

rendering.characters: expressive 2D doodle characters with bold black outlines and slightly imperfect hand-drawn linework
rendering.environment: polished painterly cartoon with cinematic depth and cohesive color grading
forbidden: generic scene that could illustrate another video
abstract theory label as the hook
headline and image pursuing different questions
hard horizontal seam below the headline

attachment_policy.attach: Only the character sheets for tokens used in the prompt.
attachment_policy.logo: Add the channel logo later in an editor, never ask the image model to draw it.

quality_gate: The headline is readable at 120 pixels wide.
The headline contains no more than four words.
The scene depicts a specific event, action, object, relationship, or consequence from the script.
The physical event is understandable without the video title.
The headline and image pursue one shared viewer question.
The image partially answers the headline with visible physical evidence.
The decisive explanation or outcome remains hidden.
Changing the headline would require changing the scene.
The headline is readable inside the same continuous illustrated scene.
No separate text band, header strip, or hard horizontal seam is present.
The mascot and cast identities match their attached sheets.
The bottom-right corner remains visually quiet.
